questions.q: What is "drift" in a GitOps context?
options: A gradual increase in cluster CPU usage over time
Any divergence between the live cluster state and the state declared in Git, typically caused by a manual change made outside the normal pipeline
The latency between a git commit and a CI build starting
A planned migration from one Kubernetes version to another
questions.explain: Drift is specifically the gap that opens up when something changes the live cluster — like a manual kubectl scale command — without that change being reflected in Git, the declared source of truth.

questions.q: How does a GitOps agent like Argo CD or Flux detect drift?
options: It only checks for drift once, immediately after the initial deployment, and never again
It relies on developers to manually report when something looks wrong
It runs a continuous reconciliation loop that repeatedly diffs live cluster state against the manifests in Git
It scans container image layers for known vulnerabilities
questions.explain: The agent runs an ongoing observe-diff-act loop, continuously comparing live state to Git, which is what catches a manual change like kubectl scale without anyone reporting it.

questions.q: What does Argo CD's "OutOfSync" status indicate?
options: That the Argo CD agent itself has crashed and needs to be restarted
That the Git repository has a merge conflict that must be resolved before any sync can run
That the CI pipeline's build step failed before producing an image
That an application's live cluster state no longer matches its Git-declared manifests
questions.explain: OutOfSync is the application-level status Argo CD surfaces specifically when it detects that live state has diverged from the desired state declared in Git.

questions.q: What does "self-healing" mean when a GitOps agent is configured for it (e.g. Argo CD's selfHeal: true)?
options: The agent automatically re-applies the Git-declared manifests to overwrite manual drift, without waiting for a human to approve the correction
The cluster automatically restarts any pod that fails its liveness probe
Developers are automatically notified by email whenever a pull request is merged
The agent automatically commits any manual kubectl change back into Git on the user's behalf
questions.explain: Self-healing means the agent, on its next reconciliation pass, automatically re-applies what's declared in Git, reverting a manual change like a kubectl scale command without any human intervention.

questions.q: What does the OpenGitOps "Continuously Reconciled" principle require?
options: That every deployment include a changelog entry
That a human manually trigger every single sync operation
That software agents continuously observe actual system state and attempt to apply the desired state, not just once at deploy time
That reconciliation only happen once per calendar quarter during a scheduled maintenance window
questions.explain: Continuously Reconciled specifically requires an ongoing, standing process of observing and correcting state, which is what distinguishes GitOps reconciliation from a one-time deploy-time check.
